title: No charges for Mountie in 2011 fatal shooting
article: AN RCMP officer who shot and killed an armed man in God's Lake First Nation last March will not face criminal charges.
The Saskatoon Police Service said Wednesday it completed its investigation into the March 2011 shooting of Paul Leonard Duck, 52.
The shooting occurred after two officers from the God's Lake Narrows RCMP detachment were guarding the scene of a house fire when they were confronted by Duck, who had a shotgun.
One officer fired at Duck and hit him twice. The man died at the local nursing station.
"The investigation and an independent Ontario Crown review have found there is no evidence to support criminal charges," said a Saskatoon Police Service release.
It is policy in Manitoba to have an external agency probe serious cases involving the RCMP.
The house fire occurred only hours before, killing Demus James and his two great-grandchildren, Kaylene Okemow, 3, and Tron Kirkness, 1.
At the time, a community member said Duck fired his shotgun into the air after two groups of youths started fighting. He began following them.
God's Lake First Nation Chief Peter Watt said he was "disappointed" by the news there would be no charges.
"Nothing new to me... I expected that," said Watt.
An inquest looking into the circumstances surrounding Duck's death will be held.
At the time of the fire, Watt said the band's firefighters and community members tried to battle the blaze without something most fire departments have: a fire truck.
Watt said at one time, the community had a fire truck, but wasn't given funding to build a fire hall to put it in. Then, when money for the fire hall was coming, the fire truck no longer worked.
